morning_soundtrack.title: Jess Williamson – “Hum Of The City”
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Jess Williamson has a voice . The Texan singer-songwriter is capable of a doing incredible things with a full-body gut wail that contains just a hint of high-lonesome yip. This isn't exactly news if you've ever spent any time listening to her, but it really comes through on her new song "Hum Of The City."
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The kind of voice that stops you mid-step on a dusty back road and makes you forget where you were going.

morning_soundtrack.title: Watch American Football Play Acoustic Cure Cover On SiriusXMU
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Reunited Midwest emo pioneers American Football have influenced a great many bands over the years. They've been back together since 2014, though they haven't always had an easy time with it , and young artists like Hayley Williams and Turnstile's Brendan Yates have lined up to work with them. While they're out there promoting their fourth album , American Football recently did an in-studio session for SiriusXMU and covered one of their own great influences, the Cure.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Like finding an old mixtape in a shoebox — two beloved eras of heartache folding into each other with quiet reverence.

morning_soundtrack.title: Star Moles Signs With Dead Oceans, Shares New Song “Born Again”
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Right now, the indie rock world is in the process of discovering Emily Moales, the prolific Philly-based New Hampshire native who records extremely cool DIY music under the name Star Moles. The Star Moles discography is deep , with dozens of releases going back nearly a decade, but the recent album Highway To Hell , one of our favorites of the year , is where most of us got on board. Jeff Tweedy covered her .
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The thrill of stumbling onto a secret that the rest of the world is just now catching up to.

morning_soundtrack.title: Star Moles Signs to Dead Oceans, Readies 2027 Tour
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Emily Moales will play U.S. headlining shows behind Highway to Hell in January
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The buzz of an underdog finally getting her moment, crackling like a venue's PA system warming up before the doors open.

morning_soundtrack.title: John Mayer Announces 2027 Las Vegas Sphere Residency [Updated]
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Each show will feature three different sets: solo, with a full band, and with the John Mayer Trio. John Mayer Announces 2027 Las Vegas Sphere Residency [Updated] Eddie Fu
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Slick, polished spectacle designed to wash over you like casino air conditioning — impressive, climate-controlled, and entirely intentional.

morning_soundtrack.title: The Monkathon: Miles Okazaki Revisits the Complete Thelonious Monk for Solo Guitar in Five-Hour Movie
morning_soundtrack.snippet: M iles Okazaki was 12 or 13 when he first heard Thelonious Monk, and the youngster was immediately struck by how the pianist disrupted convention. …
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Five hours of controlled eccentricity that rewards the patient listener like a long meditation finally breaking open.

morning_soundtrack.title: Greg Freeman Is Ready to Inspire His Devotees
morning_soundtrack.snippet: A contender for album of the year, Greg Freeman's All Set the Bone is an intense, stylistically varied testament to our grim reality, with lasting appeal.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Music that sits with you the way a late-night conversation about everything wrong with the world somehow leaves you feeling less alone.

morning_soundtrack.title: Niagara Moon Is in a Lush Mood on ‘Cool Warm Night’
morning_soundtrack.snippet: For anyone already enthralled by the cosmopolitan vibe of Niagara Moon's music, Cool Warm Night , the sixth and latest one, is the best one yet.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Silk curtains billowing in a hotel window at midnight, somewhere in a city that still knows how to dress for dinner.

morning_soundtrack.title: Ayanna Witter-Johnson Brilliantly Re-Contextualises Jazz
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Art needs new, refined voices to add a different dimension to the project as a whole. Ayanna Witter-Johnson is one such formidable bastion.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Jazz seen through a prism — familiar light refracted into colors you didn't know were hiding there.

morning_soundtrack.title: Podcast 564: John Leventhal
morning_soundtrack.snippet: The great John Leventhal joins us once again to talk about the making of his new solo album, National Drift. https://www.instagram.com/johnleventhal/ We talk about his recording process for the album, how the songs came to be, the guitars he’s currently loving, the perils of compression, and so much more. Above photo: Rosanne Cash Subscribe The post Podcast 564: John Leventhal first appeared on Fretboard Journal .
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The warm, unhurried satisfaction of watching a master craftsman explain exactly why the details no one else notices matter most.

global_silver_linings.title: Good News in History, October 8
global_silver_linings.snippet: 81 years ago toady, the microwave oven was patented by Percy Spencer. The self-taught engineer from Howland, Maine, employed by Raytheon at the time, noticed that microwaves from an active radar set he was working on started to melt a Mr. Goodbar candy bar he had in his pocket. The first food deliberately cooked with […]
global_silver_linings.reason: History is full of quiet turning points and acts of courage worth remembering — pausing to mark them reminds us that progress has always been possible, even in difficult times.

global_silver_linings.title: ‘Are you alright, boys?’: Single woman calls out men for not asking any questions on dates
global_silver_linings.snippet: Here's an easy, research-based method to be absolutely charming on your first date.
global_silver_linings.reason: A candid, good-humoured conversation about emotional reciprocity is sparking real reflection on how we show up for one another — small shifts in awareness like this are how social norms quietly improve.

global_silver_linings.title: How NYC Students Saved School Lunch
global_silver_linings.snippet: There were three clear reasons why Leslie Gomez Rivera avoided the cafeteria at her high school in Brooklyn: She didn’t like the food, the room felt hectic and there was a stigma attached to eating school meals. She preferred the library, where she could talk with friends, although sometimes that...
global_silver_linings.reason: When students are given a genuine voice in decisions that affect their lives, they step up with creativity and purpose — this story is a reminder that young people can reshape institutions from the inside out.

global_silver_linings.title: Berlin mapped 900,000 street trees. Now 12,000 people water them.
global_silver_linings.snippet: BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM Amanda Gläser-Bligh named her street tree Linda. Linda is a linden, eight years old, growing outside Gläser-Bligh’s apartment building in Charlottenburg, and once a week during Berlin’s hot months, Gläser-Bligh makes a couple of trips up and down the stairs with a watering can until she has carried 20 […] The post Berlin mapped 900,000 street trees. Now 12,000 people water them.
global_silver_linings.reason: Berlin's street-tree map turned urban nature into a shared responsibility, and 12,000 volunteers answered the call — proof that when people can see a need clearly, community care follows naturally.

discovery_articles.title: Researchers May Have Directly Glimpsed an Exoplanet’s Magnetic Field for the First Time, Building Hope of Peering Deeper Into Faraway Worlds
discovery_articles.snippet: Radio signals emanating from Beta Pictoris b suggest that this young and massive exoplanet has a strong magnetic field and intense auroral show
discovery_articles.ferns_note: A planet 63 light-years away may be throwing auroral light shows that dwarf anything our own skies have ever conjured — and we're picking up the radio whispers of it here on Earth. It's the closest we've come to eavesdropping on another world's invisible shield.

discovery_articles.title: Like a Mythical Phoenix, This Planet May Have Risen From the Ashes of a Dead Star
discovery_articles.snippet: The “second-generation” world, predicted from telescope data, could be the first known planet of its kind, and it may shed light on the future of our own solar system
discovery_articles.ferns_note: This planet is theorized to have coalesced from the wreckage of a star that died and then exploded — meaning it was, in a sense, born twice. It's an uncomfortable mirror for our own solar system's eventual fate, dressed up as a cosmic curiosity.

discovery_articles.title: Gene therapy and special goggles give some blind people limited sight
discovery_articles.snippet: Optogenetics, recognized by the 2026 medicine Nobel, makes cells respond to light, including eye cells that normally relay signals to the brain.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Researchers reprogrammed eye cells that had never been meant to sense light, then handed someone a pair of goggles — and shapes began to emerge from the dark for the first time in years. The Nobel committee called it; the patients experienced it as something closer to a quiet miracle.

featured_read.title: Three Years After October 7, I Moved Back to Nahal Oz
featured_read.snippet: But if Israel’s election doesn’t bring change, I don’t see a future for my family here.
featured_read.blurb: A mother weighs whether to rebuild her life in the Israeli kibbutz scarred by October 7, holding two impossible things at once: the pull of home and the math of survival. It's a dispatch about grief, politics, and the specific courage it takes to stay.

reading_room.title: Something Like People
reading_room.blurb: A poem worth sitting with slowly, the kind that earns its title by the last line.

reading_room.title: Evolution of Manhattan
reading_room.snippet: From Lenape land to sprawling metropolis, this detailed timelapse animation captures the making of Manhattan - by Aeon Video Watch on Aeon
reading_room.blurb: Four centuries of erasure, ambition, and accident compressed into a single animation — a reminder that every street grid on Manhattan was once a decision someone made, and before that, a life someone lived.

reading_room.title: Meet the New Otterlike Predator That Scurried Alongside Dinosaurs
reading_room.snippet: Its unique throat paved the way for our big brains
reading_room.blurb: A tiny, otter-like creature that slipped through the age of dinosaurs turns out to hold a clue to how mammals grew the brains we're using right now to read this sentence. The evolutionary leap runs straight through its throat.

reading_room.title: Tuesdays with the guys
reading_room.snippet: In the wake of an unexpected tragedy, I decided to rethink my male friendships - by Rajeev Balasubramanyam Read on Psyche
reading_room.blurb: After an unexpected death forces him to look honestly at his male friendships, Rajeev Balasubramanyam asks what men actually owe each other — and what goes quietly unspoken until it's too late. A quiet reckoning with the shape of modern male intimacy.

reading_room.title: She Died at the San Diego Border. A Surveillance Camera Was in Plain Sight.
reading_room.snippet: "In Southern California’s Otay Mountain Wilderness, the federal surveillance network seems unavoidable. But year after year, migrant deaths persist."
reading_room.blurb: Cameras cover every ridge of the Otay Mountain Wilderness, yet people keep dying there unseen — this piece sits with the bitter paradox of a surveillance state that watches everything and prevents nothing. A devastating look at what it means to be monitored but not protected.
